# Changelog

All notable changes to AxonFlow will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Each entry is grouped by edition: **Community** changes also ship in the
community mirror, **Enterprise** changes are EE-only.

---

## [11.0.0] - 2026-09-15 (one anchored engine authors the verdict on the enforcement planes it governs, typed policy authoring ships in the portal, and the legacy policy planes retire to a read surface)


### Known issues

- On deployments that run the optional AxonFlow gateway adapters in front of agentgateway, an organization whose PII detection action is set to redact has requests carrying personal data refused with `unsupported_obligation` instead of redacted, on the MCP, LLM and HTTP authorization routes; v11.0.1 fixes this. Deployments that do not run the gateway adapters are not affected.
- On a fresh install, governed requests may be refused for up to 30 seconds after first boot while the policy cache catches up with the migrations; v11.0.1 closes it.

### Security

- **`/api/v1/mcp/check-input` refuses a redaction it cannot discharge, `403 unsupported_obligation`, instead of answering an outage** (#4264). Under an organization's `pii=redact` posture with no capability handshake (every plugin's default), a permit composes a mandatory redaction of the request, and check-input hands back only the statement. The request pass also scans `parameters`, so when the PII sat only there (the Google ADK plugin sends a tool's name as the statement and its arguments as the parameters) the redaction masked nothing and the route answered `503 {"blocked": false}`, an outage: the Google ADK plugin fails open on a 5xx and ran the tool on the unmasked request, as any client that fails open on a 5xx would. It now answers `403` with `allowed: false` and a `block_reason` starting `unsupported_obligation:` that names the obligation, the policy that attached it and why, as decide refuses the same condition. A statement and a parameter that both carry PII are refused the same way; they were answered `200` with the statement masked and the parameter handed back unmasked. Each parameter is checked on its own, as the text the request pass scanned. A redaction the platform could not attempt stays a `503`, under an outage cause: no redaction engine installed is `enforcer_not_wired`, and anything else it could not attempt (the policies unreadable, a requirement or detector the engine no longer holds) is `evaluation_failed`. The MCP server's `check_policy` tool shares the projection, so the same refusal answers its deny result there rather than an error result. **Known limit:** check-input cannot hand back a masked parameter, so under `pii=redact` a call whose parameters carry PII is refused; v11.1.0 adds a `redacted_parameters` member (epic #4249). **Metric:** `axonflow_decision_enforce_decisions_total{plane="mcp:request",verdict="unavailable"}` no longer carries `reason="obligation_undischargeable"`; the refusal counts under `verdict="deny",reason="unsupported_obligation"`. **Shared engine:** `sharedpolicy.ParameterScanText` is the one definition of the text the request pass scans for a parameter, read by the scan and by this check. The MCP response pass's handling of the same cause is unchanged: it withholds the response.

- **The MCP server answers a Community SaaS rate limit with HTTP 429, and a hook's call counts once against the per-minute limit** (#4261). `/api/v1/mcp-server` answered both the per-minute limit and the daily quota with a 200 whose JSON-RPC result carried the rate-limit envelope in `result.content[0].text`, and the per-minute answer carried the daily envelope (`limit_type: daily_quota`, resetting at midnight UTC). The installed claude, codex and cursor hooks read an envelope only from a 429 or a 403, so they passed both answers by as ordinary results: no upgrade prompt, no throttle. Both answers are now HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`, with the envelope where the hooks read it (`result.content[0].text`, `isError: true`), so a hook now sees the limit and its `Retry-After`; what each hook does with it is in the plugins entry above. The per-minute answer carries a new `limit_type: per_minute`, window `minute`, `resets_at` a minute out, `Retry-After: 60` and a new wording, which is not one of the wordings #1958 locked. A credential that the pre-credential per-minute limiter refuses, on `initialize` or any method that authenticates, gets the same per-minute answer (with an empty `tier`, since the tier is not resolved yet) instead of `401 Authentication required`. A request with no `Mcp-Session-Id`, which is how the hooks call, is now counted once: the pre-credential limiter counted it and the tier check counted it again, so a Free tenant (25 a minute) was refused at about its 13th call. The tier check now reads that count, as the REST routes do; a cached MCP-protocol session, which skips the pre-credential limiter, is still counted by the tier check. The agent spec documents the 429, the envelope's `per_minute` type, and the JSON-RPC error codes the server sends: `-32001` for an authentication failure and the JSON-RPC 2.0 standard codes. Two things change for a reader of this surface. A native MCP client (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor connected to the server itself, not through the hooks) now gets an HTTP 429 where it got a 200 tool result, which Streamable-HTTP transports usually surface as a transport error. And the per-minute and daily answers, which were 200s, are now 4XX responses, so they count toward Community SaaS's `High4XXErrorAlarm` (the load balancer's `HTTPCode_Target_4XX_Count` above 50 in two consecutive 5-minute periods); the pre-credential refusal was already a 4XX, a 401, and is now a 429. A `tools/call` refused by the pre-credential limiter is audited as `per_minute`, and so is a rate-limited session `DELETE`, which answers 429 with `Retry-After` instead of 401. While Redis fails, the per-minute count is read from the in-memory count the limiter keeps meanwhile, on the REST routes too, instead of as zero. The OpenClaw plugin recognises the `per_minute` limit type in its own fix, tracked on #4249's plugins row and in the openclaw repository. **Repository-only parts, which do not reach the mirror:** the runtime leg in `runtime-e2e/3060_community_saas_reads/test.sh`, where a fresh Free tenant's sessionless `tools/call check_policy` calls pass 25 and the 26th gets the per-minute answer.

- **The legacy policy write routes answer the freeze before they read a body** *(Community)* (#4237, PRD v11 §1.5, §5 item 5). On a deployment where migrations/core/172 has revoked the legacy write, a body that failed validation never reached the write, so it was never answered the `409 LEGACY_POLICY_WRITE_FROZEN` that the database's refusal is classified as. The bulk imports (`POST /api/v1/policies/import`, which the agent serves through its proxy, `POST /api/v1/dynamic-policies/import` and `POST /api/v1/tenant-policies/import`) answered a bare `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and create and update (`POST` and `PUT` on `/api/v1/policies`, `/api/v1/dynamic-policies` and `/api/v1/tenant-policies`) answered `400`.

- **The agent's system-policy writes and template apply answer the freeze before they read a body** *(Community)* (#4237). The agent's system-policy create, update and toggle (`/api/v1/system-policies`, and the deprecated `/api/v1/static-policies`) and the orchestrator's `POST /api/v1/templates/{id}/apply` answered before their writes, so on a deployment whose connection may not write the legacy tables a request was answered `400`, `403`, `404`, or, for an update that changed nothing, `200`, never the freeze. Each now asks the database first (`legacyfreeze.RefuseWhenRevoked`, the one guard the orchestrator's policy routes use) and answers `409 LEGACY_POLICY_WRITE_FROZEN` naming `/api/v1/typed-policies` before the body is read, and for update and toggle before the row is looked up; an owner-role deployment still writes. Delete takes no body and still answers an unknown id (`404`) or a system-tier id (`403`) before the freeze; that is tracked on #4249.

- **The identity-compat comparison is removed** *(Community)* (PRD v11 §1.3; #3854). Legacy authentication and the identity plane no longer resolve a credential side by side: the identity plane alone decides whether a credential is admitted as a decision's subject. The comparison's adapter and recorder, its `axonflow_identity_compat_*` series (with the `reason` label #3854 added to one of them earlier in this release), its `[IDENTITY-COMPAT]` log lines, its recording rules and alerts (`identity-compat.rules.yml`), the internal `GET /api/v1/identity/internal/enforce-precondition` route and its `identity.enforce_precondition` capability are gone, and `identity_realm_refused` is no longer emitted (`RealmRefusalCode` stays reserved in the wire vocabulary). The identity-settings read-failure counter is renamed `axonflow_identity_org_settings_read_failures_total`, and its alert `AxonFlowIdentityCompatOrgSettingsUnreadable` becomes `AxonFlowIdentityOrgSettingsUnreadable` (`identity-org-settings.rules.yml`). The orchestrator no longer reads `AXONFLOW_IDENTITY_ORG_SETTINGS_TTL_SECONDS`, so an operator who set it there can drop it; the agent still reads it, for the Shared Signals opt-in. `docs/security/identity-compat-mode.md` is now the retirement page.

- **Breaking: a retired identity-compat variable refuses to boot** *(Community)* (PRD v11 §1.3, §5.1). `AXONFLOW_IDENTITY_COMPAT_MODE`, `_ENFORCE_REASONS`, `_PATHS` and `_AGREEMENT_LOG_EVERY`, set to any non-empty value (`off` included) on the agent or the orchestrator, stop the process at boot with a message naming each one set, the PRD sections and `docs/security/identity-compat-mode.md`; an empty value boots, because earlier compose files and templates pass them through empty. They are removed from the compose files, from both CloudFormation templates (the `IdentityCompatMode`, `IdentityCompatEnforceReasons`, `IdentityCompatPaths` and `IdentityCompatAgreementLogEvery` parameters, which a stack update must stop passing), from `update-stack.yml` and from `deploy-cloudformation.sh`.

- **The organization template's DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, SQL-injection and PII rows decide on `/api/request`** (#4131). Eight of the template's 22 rows carry v10 categories (`dangerous_queries`, `sql_injection`, `pii_detection`) that `migrations/core/127` never canonicalized, and `/api/request`'s category filter admitted canonical categories only, so a `DROP TABLE` through the LLM proxy was allowed with an advisory.

### Community
- **A block that an organization's recorded detection override causes names the policy that blocked** (#4211, PRD v11 §1.14). The organization root's replacement of a shipped control under a recorded override (#4045) carried no display name, so every surface that names a policy from the anchored engine's identity named none for it: `/api/v1/decide`'s `policy_identities`, and the `policy_names` of the decide, gateway pre-check, `/api/request`, OpenAI-compatible and MCP audit rows, which the portal audit view shows. The replacement now carries the shipped control's own display name; its id (`organization_override:<control>`) and description still say that an override assigned the action.
- **The orchestrator's activation answer, and the authoring API's artifact and diff reads, tell a store failure apart** (#4271). #4255 made `GET /api/v1/typed-policies/active` answer a store it could not read 503 `storage_unavailable`, with the store's error in the log only. The same class remained around it. `authoring.API.RenderDigest` returned the store's error raw beside an unsentinelled "not admitted" error; it now returns `authoring.ErrNotAdmitted` for a digest the store does not hold and wraps a store error with `%w` (`platform/decision/authoring/api.go:263`). `authoring.API.Diff` returned the store's error raw; it now marks an unreadable active document with `authoring.ErrActiveUnavailable`, so a caller tells it from the candidate's own error (`:281`). The orchestrator's `POST /api/v1/typed-policies/activate` wrote a failed read-back's raw error into its 200 body's `template_omissions_unavailable`; the answer stays 200, because the activation stands, and the field now carries a fixed sentence while the cause goes to the log (`platform/orchestrator/typed_authoring_route.go:888`).
- **`GET /api/v1/typed-policies/active` answers `503 storage_unavailable` when the typed-authoring store cannot be read, not `404 nothing_active`** (#4255). The route turned every error from `authoring.API.Render` into `404 nothing_active`, so a database read failure told an operator, through every SDK's `active()`, that their organization had no active policy document. `Render` now returns the `authoring.ErrNothingActive` sentinel for a root with nothing active and wraps the store's error otherwise. The route answers `404 nothing_active` only for the sentinel, and `503 storage_unavailable` for a store error, with the write side's "retry once the database is reachable"; the store's own error goes to the log, never the body. A workspace whose durable store could not be opened (the first request after a restart while the database is down, for one) answers the same 503: the in-process store it holds instead is empty, so it could only have answered `nothing_active`. An active document that no longer verifies on load (its signing key de-authorized, or its signature, digest or module no longer holding) answers `500 active_unverifiable` instead: an integrity fault, not a storage outage, carried by the durable store's `authoringstore.ErrArtifactUnverifiable`. A signing key this replica has not loaded, because the reload that would load it was deferred, answers `503 key_not_loaded` instead (`authoringstore.ErrSigningKeyNotLoaded`): the key may be one another replica authorized moments ago or one not authorized at all, and a retry after a few seconds usually settles which, the document then verifying or answering `500 active_unverifiable`. The orchestrator spec documents the 503 reasons, `catalog_not_configured`, `storage_unavailable` and, on `/active` only, `key_not_loaded`, as one `TypedAuthoringUnavailable` response on every typed-policies route that can answer `storage_unavailable`: `/publish` and `/activate` (which already refused a degraded store, undocumented) and `/active`. `/edition` and `/validate` answer only the first and keep `TypedAuthoringUnconfigured`. For the SDK census and the release notes: an SDK that reads "no active document" from `active()` on a 404 is correct once the route stops sending 404 for a store failure, and a `503 storage_unavailable` or `503 key_not_loaded` from `/active` is retriable. The live legs are in `runtime-e2e/1431_policy_path_alias/test.sh`: before any publish, `/active` answers `404 nothing_active` from the durable store, and with the suite's postgres stopped it answers `503 storage_unavailable`.
- **Plugins and frameworks on v11.0.0: what each of the eight public plugins can and cannot do, measured live** *(Community)* (#3746, #4249). A census drove every plugin's own code (the Claude Code, Codex and Cursor hooks and MCP entries, the Claude Desktop MCP proxy, the Google ADK plugin, the LiteLLM adapter, the n8n node and the OpenClaw plugin) against the release candidate on Community, Community SaaS and Enterprise. `docs/COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.md` carries one row per plugin.
  - **Six plugin fixes ship before the tag, one per repository:**
    - the Claude Code, Codex and Cursor hooks, pre and post, fail closed on a limit answer that carries no `allowed`; the Codex and Cursor hooks allowed every tool call, and all three passed tool output unchecked, once a Community SaaS Free tenant reached the per-minute cap (a hook call counted twice until #4261, the platform half, below): over the cap a hook now denies and shows the upgrade prompt, where it had allowed; and the Claude Code post hook no longer drops an output deny;
    - the Google ADK plugin applies the platform's masked tool result, where the model had received the original, and stops sending the per-user token as an audit `user_id`;
    - the n8n node builds its `Authorization` header on n8n 2.x, evaluates its default Idempotency Key, and stops sending its secret in request bodies;
    - the Codex MCP entry sends its credential with the `Basic` scheme.
  - **What v11 changes for every plugin:**
    - a deny names a reason code (`explicit_constraint`, `unsupported_obligation`, `unknown_constraint; ...`) and a corpus id;
    - a client declaring `[]` under a mandatory redaction obligation is denied on both editions, and the Enterprise build names `pep_capability_unsupported` (Enterprise);
    - an approval-requiring request is refused, never held, on every plane that matches it (PRD v11 §1.13), so no plugin's approval-hold branch is reachable (Enterprise);
    - a session override answers 201 and changes no v11 verdict, and the corpus id a deny names answers 404 (#4254).
  - **Platform rows from the same census:**
    - #4261 (fixed below): a limit was answered in the wrong class;
    - #4264: an undischargeable obligation on `/api/v1/mcp/check-input` answers 503 `blocked: false`;
    - #4265 (Enterprise): the MCP `list_policies` tool answers 401 on every Enterprise deployment.
  - **Known limits that ship with v11.0.0, each with a v11.1.0 issue:**
    - one refused override or 401 locks an OpenClaw session (before #4261 a 401 could be a quota);
    - the Codex hooks fail open on a plain 401;
    - the Cursor MCP entry sends no handshake;
    - the Claude Desktop proxy shows `unknown_constraint` without its reason;
    - the n8n node surfaces a deny as "Forbidden - perhaps check your credentials?" (then "Request failed with status code 403");
    - the Google ADK plugin fails open on every platform error, a 401 included; the LiteLLM adapter and OpenClaw's tool path fail open on a 429 or an unreachable platform;
    - LiteLLM fetches its model cost map from GitHub at import unless `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP` is set.
- **OJK readiness no longer counts a soft-deleted Indonesia PII policy as a configured control** (#3874). The PII Detection check on `GET /api/v1/ojk/audit/readiness`, and the active-policy count on `GET /api/v1/ojk/dashboard`, counted `static_policies` rows by `enabled` alone, so a soft-deleted row still read as a control that was set up. Both now also require `deleted_at IS NULL`, the predicate the policy loader selects by, so a policy that was deleted counts as no control. The SEBI and US securities readiness readers already applied it.
- **An activation lists each policy it enforces, and one package builds an organization's activation inputs** (#4152, #4254). Groundwork, with no API change. `Activation.PolicyEffects` lists every policy an activation enforces on its scope, and each shipped control the organization's document disabled there: its source and version as a decision names it, the shipped control it is or replaces, the legacy action it enforces and its census category and severity. The action is read through `legacycompile.LegacyActionOf`, the inverse of the one action mapping. `platform/shared/activationinputs` builds an organization's activation inputs for any plane and phase, and the orchestrator's typed-authoring dry run takes its inputs from it.
- **Breaking: `/api/request` is one anchored pass; its tier-engine second pass, the `proxy_tier` plane and the route's segment gate are removed** *(Community)* (#4253, PRD v11 §1 item 1, §1.2). `/api/request` ran a second pass whenever the anchored engine approved: the tier-aware engine, over `static_policies`' stored action column and the organization's legacy per-policy overrides (`policy_overrides`), which refused or held the request under `engine=legacy`, reason `proxy_tier_policy`. It is deleted, and with it the `proxy_tier` plane: `platform/decision/legacycompile` models eleven planes. **A legacy per-policy override (block or require_approval) no longer decides `/api/request` from v11.0.0; the effective-policies read keeps showing it under the deprecated surface (§1.11).** What the retired pass read from a shipped row's stored action column is kept on `proxy_request`, the plane that inherits the pass (`PlaneSpec.EnforcesRetiredTierPassRead`, recorded as `retired_tier_pass_action`), in two arms. A system row's stored block is enforced as block there, which binds the four `sys_admin_*` controls: their only binding was `proxy_tier`, and `/api/request` now admits their category, `security-admin`, on this plane alone. So a request naming `audit_log`; `config_`, `admin_` or `system_`; `information_schema`, `pg_catalog` or `mysql.user`; or the whole word `users` is refused by the anchored engine naming that control's `:block` policy, as the tier engine refused it, administrators included. An organization-template row keeps its stored action wherever it outranks the row's phase resolution: the corpus compiles a template row to one policy, its most restrictive plane compilation, and for nine rows that compilation was the tier plane's read of the stored column. They are the template's DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE and two SQL-injection refusals and its five redactions (`pii_ssn_detection` and the four `eu_gdpr_*` rows). All nine ship exactly as before, with the same ids and bindings less the retired plane. Every other shipped control the tier engine refused already binds block on `proxy_request`. An organization's own legacy `static_policies` rows, segment-scoped ones included, stop deciding here too: the tier engine was their last deciding reader, and they already decided nothing on every other enforcing scope (see the entry on an organization's own legacy static rows); import and activate them through the typed path. The segment gate that fed the second pass goes with it: the agent's pass on `/api/request` resolves no governance segments, a segment-store outage refuses nothing at that pass, and `axonflow_segment_policy_fail_closed_total`, which could no longer move, is removed; a request it forwards to the orchestrator's `/api/v1/process` or `/api/v1/plan/execute` is still evaluated by its dynamic policies, which resolve the user's segments and refuse when resolution fails, until the orchestrator's planes cut over. Every response and audit row on the route carries `engine=anchored`, and the enforce-decision counter records no `engine="legacy"` series. The compiler's second static read path and its `read_path_action_divergence` reason go with the plane. The system corpus, the shipped-posture table and the detector census are regenerated from a real capture: `proxy_tier` leaves every scope binding, the two `:warn` variants bound to it alone (`sys_pii_passport`, `sys_pii_singapore_postal`) leave the corpus, no surviving control's id changes, and `policy_test`, dynamic-only since this change, leaves every binding compiled from a plane's static read. #4131's discharge bindings name every declared scope, `map` and `wcp` included, so `policy_test` stays in them until the orchestrator's `policy_test` plane retires (#4258). The live proof is `runtime-e2e/3564_per_plane_enforcement/test.sh` P1b.
- **`POST /api/policies/test` previews the anchored pass it tests** *(Community)* (#4253, PRD v11 §1 item 10). It previewed two legacy passes and resolved the governance segments of the body's `user_email`. It is now a dry run of `/api/request`'s one pass for the authenticated credential: the same detector evaluation and the same enforcing seam, recording no decision (no `audit_logs` row, no enforce-decision count, no circuit-breaker violation, no signed decision; the shared engine's evaluation that feeds it still counts in its metrics, and a matched block is logged to `policy_violations` where its audit queue is wired, as before). It decides for the credential (`subject_type=Client`); on Enterprise, where `/api/request` requires a user token, that is the credential's service identity, as decide decides a token-less caller, and an organization whose posture requires a user token is refused 401, as decide refuses it. `user_email` is accepted and ignored, `segments_resolved` is no longer in the response, the response gains `engine`, `subject_type` and `policy_bundle`, and it answers 503 where the anchored engine cannot decide. The handler reads the authentication `apiAuthMiddleware` stored rather than authenticating again, which would admit the service principal twice.
  - **Admission.** `sharedpolicy.LegacyTemplateCategories()` is admitted on `/api/request` and on its policy-test surface (`/api/policies/test`), which evaluates the same category list, and on no other plane. The stored categories are not rewritten, so decide, the gateway pre-check, the OpenAI-compatible route and MCP are unchanged; binding the template on those planes is a posture decision (#4230).
  - **Case.** Stored patterns in the SQL-injection and destructive-command families (`security-sqli`, `security-dangerous` and the two v10 spellings) now match regardless of case, so `DROP TABLE` matches `drop\s+table`. This applies to an organization's own rows in those categories as well as the shipped ones. Every other family keeps its stored case; six template rows that miss their trigger only on case are recorded on #4231.
  - **A template redaction binds where a scope can carry it out.** A template `redact` row now ships as a `redact` policy bound to the scopes that can discharge a redaction (decide and the gateway pre-check through a caller that declares it, MCP, the orchestrator response and cowork ingest) and a `warn` policy on the scopes that cannot (`/api/request`, the OpenAI-compatible route). Before, `eu_gdpr_cross_border_pii` bound a mandatory redaction on `/api/request` and the OpenAI-compatible route, so every request it matched was refused `unsupported_obligation`. The template is now 22 controls in 27 policies. The `redact` halves of the four PII rows are admitted on no scope today; the posture table names each as dormant until #4230.
  - **The template's SQL keyword rows match whole words only (`migrations/core/185`).** Four patterns core/010 seeded lacked a word boundary, so once they bound on `/api/request` they would have refused ordinary text: `sql_injection_or`'s second `or`/`and` matched the end of a field name (measured: `... WHERE region = 'EU' AND color = 'red' AND brand = 'acme'`), and `union\s+select`, `drop\s+table` and `truncate\s+table` matched inside words (`the reunion selection committee met`, `backdrop tablet stand`, `truncate tables to 10 rows`). Each gains `\b` where a word must start or end. The migration rewrites a pattern only where it equals the shipped literal, so an organization's unedited copy is fixed and an edited one is left alone; an organization's own row that typed the same literal gets the same fix. Every injection and destructive statement the rows caught still matches. Whole-word prose (`Did the union select a new leader?`) still matches, the limit of a keyword pattern, and `sql_injection_or`'s recall gap (`1 OR 1=1`, `admin' AND 1=1 AND 'a'='a`) remains; both are #4231.
  - **The shipped-posture table lists a template policy only where it binds.** It listed all 22 on every scope; the implicit bundle has always composed the template restricted to the scope.
  - **Activation refuses a shipped template control a scope cannot discharge**, as it already refused a system one.
  - **Changed ids:** the five template redaction rows now ship as `<id>:redact` and `<id>:warn` (for example `corpus:static_policies:pii__ssn__detection:redact`). A document seeded from the template before this change carries the old, unsplit id, which is no longer a template id and is judged as the organization's own policy; re-seed such a draft.
  - **Changed for readers of `template_omissions`:** the publish and activation report counts template POLICIES (27) and says so, since a document carrying one half of a split control drops it on the other half's scopes.
  - **Repository-only parts, which do not reach the mirror:** `ee/platform/customer-portal/api/typed_authoring.go` (the portal's authoring dry run reads `legacycompile.ScopeDeliveries`, the one statement of what a scope's wire delivers; behaviour unchanged), `ee/platform/policy/legacyimport/plan.go` and `ee/platform/policy/legacyimport/plan_test.go` (a comment, and the test's census pin of `drop_table_prevention`'s pattern moved to core/185's), and the 3564 suite: `runtime-e2e/3564_per_plane_enforcement/test.sh`, `runtime-e2e/3564_per_plane_enforcement/README.md` and its row in `scripts/e2e/runtime_e2e_suites.tsv`.
  - **The guard.** Where the connection the write goes through may not write `dynamic_policies`, these routes answer `409 LEGACY_POLICY_WRITE_FROZEN` naming `/api/v1/typed-policies` before the body is read, whatever it contains. The database is asked per request (`legacyfreeze.MayWrite`: `has_table_privilege` on that connection), not the environment. An owner-role deployment, whose writes core/172 does not refuse, still writes. A privilege probe that cannot be answered falls through to the write, whose refusal is still classified as before.
  - **Order.** Authentication is answered first: a missing tenant is still `401` on every route, and a missing organization is `401 ORG_REQUIRED` on the imports, and in neither case is the database asked. Create and update require only the tenant, as before; through the agent the organization is always set from the credential.
  - **Validation.** The six handler sites that tested `*ValidationError` by concrete type use `errors.As`, so a wrapped validation failure on an owner-role deployment is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, not `500`.
  - **Observability.** Each pre-read refusal logs one line starting `[legacyfreeze] legacy write refused before its request body was read:` with the organization, the tenant and the route, so refusals are countable per organization.
  - **One definition.** `legacyfreeze.Refuse` answers with the message `legacyfreeze.Answer` sends; the orchestrator's sample seed asks `legacyfreeze.MayWrite` rather than its own query.
  - **Specs.** The `LegacyPolicyWriteFrozen` responses state the before-body refusal, and no longer say `AXONFLOW_DB_USE_APP_ROLE=false` decides which deployments the revoke binds: that is a property of the database connection.
  - **The agent's system-policy create, update and toggle, and the orchestrator's template apply,** refuse the same way; see the next entry.
  - **Repository-only parts, which do not reach the mirror:** `ee/examples/policies-export-import/http/policies-export-import.sh` accepts the 409; `runtime-e2e/3039_rls_blind_reads/test.sh` and its row in `scripts/e2e/runtime_e2e_suites.tsv` assert the 409 with the typed route for realistic, malformed and empty bodies on import, create and update.
  - **Repository-only parts, which do not reach the mirror:** `runtime-e2e/3039_rls_blind_reads/test.sh` and its row in `scripts/e2e/runtime_e2e_suites.tsv` (section 12's create, update, toggle and template-apply legs), and `platform/testutil/refcensus/exemption_list.go` (the three test files that drive the retired routes to prove the refusal).
- **An organization's typed document controls the shipped set, control by control** (#3746, PRD v11 §1.5). A new `system_controls` section of the authoring document names a shipped system control by its corpus id (`corpus:<table>:<row>`, the 85 controls the shipped-posture table lists) and either leaves it out (`enabled: false`) or gives it another action (`block`, `redact`, `warn` or `log`). It beats the recorded category posture on the same control and applies on every plane.
  - **Validation.** Five save-time codes: `SYSTEM_CONTROLS_OUTSIDE_ORGANIZATION`, `SYSTEM_CONTROL_UNKNOWN`, `SYSTEM_CONTROL_DUPLICATE`, `SYSTEM_CONTROL_MALFORMED`, and `SYSTEM_CONTROL_NOT_REACTIONABLE`: a shipped dynamic control may be left out but not re-actioned (#4187). The diff classifies each change by its effect.
  - **Activation.** The section folds by control id after the scope restriction and before the category posture. A left-out control's policies are removed on every scope. A re-actioned one is replaced on the organization root by `organization_control:<policy id>`, carrying the shipped policy's name and the document's version. The activation reports what the section did on each scope.
  - **No `api_version` change.** A document that names no control is byte-identical to one written before the section existed.
  - **The dry runs read the posture.** Both transports' publication and activation dry runs read the organization's recorded detection posture, uncached, and refuse when it cannot be read, as the enforcing seam does. The category-to-policy fan-out has one source, `policy.OrgOverrideReach`, which the agent, the orchestrator and the portal all read.
  - **Internal API change.** `activation.Activator` now takes `func(context.Context) (Inputs, error)`, and an error it returns refuses the activation. `authoring.NewDocument` now takes the document whole: `NewDocument(Document, *Catalog)`. Both transports follow both changes, and so must any caller outside this tree.
  - **The orchestrator's typed route signs every member it is sent.** It rebuilt each document from its metadata and policy, so a `system_controls` section was neither validated nor signed there. The publish still answered 200 with a new digest, and the organization was decided exactly as before; runtime-e2e 3564 measured this. `NewDocument` now carries the authored document whole and re-derives only `api_version` and the interactive realms. The portal always handed the document on whole.
  - **The shipped system view names each policy's control.** It adds `control` and `dynamic`, so a client groups the 118 shipped policies into their 85 controls without re-deriving an id.
  - **The legacy lever.** `policy_overrides` stays writable for ADR-044 break-glass; its per-policy handlers still answer 409.
- **Legacy per-policy overrides are imported once, into an unpublished draft** (#3746, PRD v11 §1.5, `migrations/core/183`). On its first boot after the migrations, the agent translates each organization's `policy_overrides` rows into a draft: the shipped organization template plus a `system_controls` section.
  - **The record.** It is written to `typed_policy_import_drafts`, one row per organization with any override, under forced RLS. A trigger admits only a one-time dismissal, so the upgrade never imports twice. `draft_digest` is the digest an authored document gets.
  - **What is carried.** Only rows that are organization-wide, unrevoked, unexpired and not break-glass (a tool signature, or the action `allow`), and that change a shipped control. Rows that disagree about one control are skipped. Every entry passes the save-time checks an authored one does, and every skipped row is recorded with its reason or code.
  - **What it does not do.** It publishes and activates nothing. The legacy tables are read by the owner-only `typed_policy_import_candidates()`, so no Go reader of them is added.
- **`docker-compose.otel-grafana.yml` starts again on top of `docker-compose.yml`** *(Community)* (#4148). #3068 bound the base file's Prometheus and Grafana to `127.0.0.1:9090` and `127.0.0.1:3000`. The overlay's own `9090:9090` and `3000:3000` were concatenated onto the same services, so each bound its host port twice and the observability stack failed to start. The overlay now leaves those two ports to the base file's localhost bindings.
- **Community SaaS organizations registered before this release get the same audited `sqli=block`, once, at deploy** (#4017). `migrations/community-saas/182` records the override, updated_by `system:community-saas/182`, and one `DETECTION_POSTURE_SET` `admin_audit_log` row for every live `cs_` registration. It runs in a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by `axonflow_platform_admin`, so row-level security cannot hide a registration from it, and it warns if its owner cannot bypass that. An organization that already chose a sqli action keeps it, a terminated registration or one outside the `cs_` fence is left alone, a second run changes nothing, and its down withdraws only the overrides it recorded that nobody has changed since. `scripts/migrations/dry-run-community-saas-182.sh` applies the file inside a transaction it rolls back, so an operator sees, organization by organization, what the deploy will record.
- **A policy pack detector is validated only by the validator its source names** *(Community)* (#4141, PRD v11 §1.9). A pack source's detector gains an optional `validator`, a key of the detector layer's validator registry (`passport`, `phone`, ...). A detector that names none matches its pattern as written. It no longer takes the validator the loader resolves for a row from its category or from a PII-type token in its id, which gated every `pii-india` detector by the Aadhaar checksum and an id carrying `bank_account` by a US routing checksum. An unknown name refuses boot, as a pattern RE2 cannot compile does. The FinCrime pack's detectors resolved no validator either way, and match as they did.
- **A banking deployment mode installs the banking policy packs** *(Community)* (#4141, PRD v11 §1.9). The agent installs the packs `AXONFLOW_POLICY_PACKS` names plus the packs its deployment mode installs; a pack named both ways is installed once. A mode that applies the `industry/banking` migrations, `in-vpc-banking` or `saas`, installs `mas-feat`, `rbi` and `sebi` (`industryPolicyPacks` in `platform/agent/policy_packs.go`); every other mode installs none by mode. A Community build in such a mode refuses boot, naming the mode and §1.9, as it refuses a named pack: the image carries none.
- **A policy pack detector can take a different action on requests and on responses, and a pack may redact** *(Community)* (#4141, PRD v11 §1.9).
  - **Per-phase actions.** A pack source's detector gains optional `action_request` and `action_response`, as a `static_policies` row has. Each overrides `action` for its phase.
  - **How a detector compiles.** A detector whose phases resolve to one action still compiles to ONE control under its unsuffixed id, bound on its own phase. That is every existing pack control, and the committed FinCrime document is byte-identical. A detector whose two phases differ compiles to one control per phase, `pack:<pack>:<detector>:<action>`, the shipped corpus's own split-variant naming. Both variants read the one detector.
  - **Binding.** Activation binds each pack control on the scopes of its own phase (`Pack.ControlPhase`). A pack mirroring the shipped PII posture therefore warns on the request scopes and redacts on the response scopes, where the agent loads pack detectors.
  - **Redact.** A pack's `redact` now compiles. Its obligation targets the plane's content root, as every shipped redact control's does, and the control's description says so. That caveat, `redact_target_not_stored`, is the one a pack may state; any other still refuses the pack.
  - **The legacy engine** carries the detector's action per phase.
- **The seed-writer census reads the mirror's shape before judging a rule stale** *(Community)* (#4126). On the community mirror, `TestNoStaticPoliciesWriterOutsideARuledClass` failed its stale-rule direction for four rules whose writers the sync strips: the runtime suite fixtures, the readiness-gate fixtures, the #4138 seed bundle and `scripts/v9_rollback/094_rollback.sql`. On the mirror's shape (no `ee/` tree) that direction is now reported as not run, with the reason. Every writer the mirror carries is still classified, and the capped class still holds its cap. The enterprise tree judges every rule exactly on every pull request and keeps the exact check.
- **An organization can withdraw its typed document and return to the shipped set** (PRD v11 §1.15, #3746). A withdrawal is an appended activation of kind `withdraw`, with a reason and an actor, after which the organization is decided exactly as one that never published anything is: the decision carries the same implicit `policy_bundle`, byte for byte, and the policy epoch still advances. It names the digest of the shipped organization template, because the composed implicit bundle has no single digest, and it chains onto the document it withdrew; a promotion afterwards starts from nothing active and chains onto the withdrawal. Nothing is deleted. Migration `core/184` admits the kind in the ledger and the audit table, each with a required reason, and its down keeps every withdraw row while refusing a new one. `authoring.API.Withdraw` runs the same two production checks as rollback, including a dry run of the implicit bundle it restores.
- **Every typed decision names what decided it** (#4127, PRD v11 §1.14). `/api/v1/decide` answers `policy_identities` beside `evaluated_policies`, one entry per id in the same order: the policy's own display name where it has one, whose it is (`shipped`, `organization` or `pack`), and, for an organization's own policy or an installed pack's, the version it was published at. A shipped control carries no version, because `policy_bundle` already identifies it. `document_version` names the organization's active document and is omitted under the implicit baseline. `evaluated_policies` is unchanged, so nothing an SDK reads today moves. The audit row of every typed decision (decide, the gateway pre-check, `/api/request`, the OpenAI-compatible route and the MCP response pass) carries the same names in `policy_names`, each policy's source in `policy_sources`, the published versions in `policy_versions`, `document_version`, and the requested action's display name in `action_name`. Before this a typed policy's row carried its id with no name and no version, the MCP response pass recorded a refusing constraint's id as its display name on `resources/query` and `tools/execute`, and a `check-output` refusal recorded no name. The runtime leg is `runtime-e2e/3347_audit_display_names/test.sh`, which publishes a named constraint and reads its name and version back from the decide response and the audit row.
- **A deny because a constraint could not be evaluated names that constraint and the attribute** *(Community)* (#4227, PRD v11 §1.14). A request the engine refused as `unknown_constraint` was answered with the bare code and an empty `evaluated_policies`, so neither the caller nor the operator could tell which policy refused it or what was missing. On an indeterminate deny, the constraints that could not be evaluated are now the policies that decided it, binding first, on every anchored plane. `/api/v1/decide` keeps `unknown_constraint` as the first entry of `reasons` and adds one per constraint, starting with its id: `ceiling.refund (organization, document version 1) could not be evaluated: no value was supplied for args.request_type, which the document requires`. `evaluated_policies` and `policy_identities` list those constraints first, then what matched, so on this deny `evaluated_policies` carries ids where it carried `[]`; on every other decision it is unchanged. The gateway pre-check's and `/api/request`'s `block_reason`, the OpenAI-compatible route's refusal, the MCP request pass's `block_reason` on `check-input` and `check_policy`, a connector route's `Request blocked:` error and the MCP response pass's refusal keep the `unknown_constraint` prefix and gain the same text after `; `. The pre-check's `policies`, `/api/request`'s matched policies, `check_policy`'s `blocked_by`, the response pass's blocking policy, the audit row and the connector query audit's `request_matched_policies` name the binding constraint first. A deny another policy decided while a constraint was also unknown names only what decided it. The breaker tests are Enterprise-only (`platform/agent/unknown_constraint_breaker_test.go`), since the Community breaker records nothing, and the live leg is Phase E7 of `runtime-e2e/3564_per_plane_enforcement/test.sh`. An `unknown_constraint` deny still records no circuit-breaker violation on any plane. It named no policy before, so none was recorded, and it is a data or availability outcome, not a violation by the caller. An `unknown_requirement` deny, the same kind of outcome, no longer records one either; on decide, the gateway pre-check and `/api/request` it named the permissions that matched and was recorded against them. On `/api/v1/decide`, the top-blocked-policies metric now labels such a deny by its binding constraint where it read `unknown`: a shipped control by its id, an organization's or a pack's constraint as `tenant_custom`. A deny with no blocking policy, including an allow the obligation gates turn into a deny, is labelled by the first policy it names under the same rule, so an organization's id is never a label. No field is added.
- **The MCP response pass names the policy packs that composed into its bundle, as `/api/v1/decide` does** *(Community)* (#4196, PRD v11 §1.9). A pack whose control binds on the MCP response pass is now named by digest as `policy_packs` (`<pack id>@<digest of the instantiated pack document>`, sorted) on `/api/v1/mcp/check-output`, on the `resources/query` and `tools/execute` success bodies and those routes' response-pass refusals, on the MCP server's `check_output` tool's allowed and blocked results (and, on Enterprise, its redaction refusal), and on the canonical audit row each one writes. The MCP request pass has done this since #4216. The response pass recorded its bundle and never its packs, so the field was missing on that pass's wire and rows. The field is omitted when no pack binds, so a deployment with no pack sees no change. The OpenAPI `MCPCheckOutputResponse`, `MCPQueryResponse` and `MCPExecuteResponse` schemas document it, and the pack READMEs (`ee/policy-packs/fincrime/README.md`, `ee/policy-packs/sebi/README.md`) now say which MCP passes name each pack (FinCrime's request-phase `fincrime` controls never bind on the response pass). The live leg is `runtime-e2e/4141_banking_policy_packs/test.sh`, which asserts the RBI pack's digest on the `check-output` wire and on its canonical row in the same run. A comment in `platform/agent/pep_handshake_enforce_community.go` also says what it had wrong: a mandatory obligation the enforcement point cannot discharge is refused `unsupported_obligation` on every edition wherever the engine composes it (`composeSet`), and wherever `/api/v1/decide` or the gateway pre-check attaches a checksum validator's redaction (`attachValidatorRedactions`). The handler-level refusals, the naming and counting of the capability gap, and the MCP passes' refusal of a validator's masking (`applyMCPRedactionRefusal`) are Enterprise-only. A census of `docs/api/agent-api.yaml` and `docs/api/orchestrator-api.yaml` for `segment_resolution_failed`, `segment_identity_unresolved` and `ADR-060` found seven `agent-api.yaml` paragraphs that still documented a governance-segment gate the anchored engine removed: the pre-check's example and its `policies` reserved value, the `/api/v1/decide` 403, the `check-input` and `check-output` 403s, the MCP server's governance-segments note, and the connector query and execute 403. Each now says the cause is retired, the example the pre-check can no longer return is removed, and a comment in `platform/agent/decision_handler.go` no longer lists it as a security event decide sets. The MCP server's identity notes that followed the segment note now say what the code does without it (a shared synthetic identity is refused only a per-user session override), and the `/api/v1/decide` 403 also lists the token-tenant mismatch it answers. The orchestrator's segment refusals are live and unchanged.
- **The MCP request pass is decided by the anchored engine, the sixth enforcing scope** *(Community)* (#3564, #3746, PRD v11 §1.2, §1.13). `POST /api/v1/mcp/check-input`, the MCP server's `check_policy` tool, and the connector `query` and `execute` routes before the tool runs are decided on `mcp:request` through the enforcing seam the other scopes use. `/health`'s `enforcing_planes` names `mcp:request`, and each response and audit row on the pass carries `engine`, `subject_type` and `policy_bundle`. The shared engine's request pass is now detector input only. The pass also names the policy packs that bound, as `policy_packs` (`<pack id>@<digest>`), on `check-input`, `check_policy`, a connector route's refusal and every audit row it writes, exactly as `/api/v1/decide` does; the query and execute success bodies are the response pass's wire and are not changed here (part of #4196). Every audit row the pass writes also names what decided it (PRD v11 §1.14, #4186): each policy it matched by its display name, whose it is and the version it was published at, the active document's version and the action's display name, from the same identities `/api/v1/decide` reads, which are now the one source of the names on the pass's rows and bodies.
  - **Masking follows the decision.** `check-input` and `check_policy` hand back the statement masked by exactly the redaction requirements the decision matched. The shipped posture binds this pass's PII controls as advisory (`warn`, `log`), so a PII statement is allowed and handed back unmasked unless the organization records `pii=redact`, which masks it.
  - **The connector routes discharge nothing.** `query` and `execute` run the statement themselves, so a permit carrying an obligation is refused `unsupported_obligation`.
  - **A request the engine cannot decide is refused** (PRD v11 §1.7): 503 on the REST routes, an error naming the cause on `check_policy`, and an `error` audit row on both.
  - **A challenge answers `approval_required`, naming the plane** (PRD v11 §1.13): the MCP passes have no hold.
  - **Removed with the engines they belonged to** (no compatibility promise, PRD v11 §1.3). An active ADR-044 session override no longer turns a block into an allow on `check-input` or the MCP server's `check_policy` and `check_output` tools, and no `override_used` event is written there. The request pass no longer requires a per-user token because a segment-scoped policy is in scope (#3430). Legacy FinCrime no longer decides the request pass; its seeded rows still run in the detector pass, where they decide nothing. Removed at base `e18bc311f`: `platform/agent/mcp_richer_context.go:381` (`applyOverrideToCheckInputBlock`) and `:424` (`writeOverrideUsedEvent`), called from `platform/agent/mcp_handler.go:3541` and `platform/agent/mcp_server_handler.go:1945` and `:2174`; `platform/agent/mcp_identity.go:331`, `:410` and `:468` (the segment gate) and `platform/shared/policy/engine.go:768` (`HasSegmentScopedPolicies`); `platform/agent/mcp_handler.go:1056` (`redactInputStatement`).
- **The corpus compiler no longer declares a loaded dynamic row unenforced because its `description` or `category` is NULL** (#4078). `legacycompile`'s scan-drop model for `dynamic_policies` listed `description` and `category` as columns whose NULL fails `RefreshDynamicPolicies`' scan, reasoning from the schema. The loader COALESCEs both in its query, so such a row loads and is enforced. The model now lists every column the reader selects without COALESCE into a destination that cannot hold NULL. `TestScanDropModelsMatchTheLoaderQueries` compares all three models with `platform/shared/policy/loader.go`'s queries and scans, and fails when a model and its reader part. Reading the reader found a real gap in the runtime model as well. `static_policies.metadata` is nullable JSONB scanned into a `json.RawMessage`, which database/sql cannot fill with a NULL, so a NULL-metadata row fails `loadFromDatabase`'s scan and is enforced nowhere. The model now lists it, and `TestLoaderDropsARowWhoseMetadataIsNull` pins the drop. The compiler judges every modelled column NULL-or-absent from the raw row, not a hand-kept list, and the guard fails on a scan type or a SELECT item it cannot classify. No shipped artifact changes: against a fresh capture of a migrated database, `TestRegenerateTheShippedCorpusArtifact` and the shipped-posture derivation both pass byte-identically. The two rows the model misdescribed, `sensitive_data_control` and `high_risk_block`, had already left the corpus with `core/179` and `core/160`. `technical-docs/designs/DETECTOR_REGISTRY_DESIGN.md` §7 records the two decisions taken on 2026-09-13: the 010-generation cleanup is v11.1.0, and v11.0.0 publishes `security-admin` unchanged.
- **The India PII detector no longer reads an email address as a UPI id** (#4225). The UPI pattern stopped at the first dot after the `@`, so `jane.doe@acme.com` reached the Community build's email filter as the handle `acme`, passed it, and was reported as a UPI id. The pattern now carries the whole domain, and a handle with a dot or a hyphen is refused as a mail domain, a rule that replaces the TLD and full-domain lists for every TLD. A real VPA followed by a space, a full stop and a space, a comma or a line end matches as before, and so does one in a `upi://pay?pa=` link; one glued to the next word by a dot or a hyphen (`rahul@okicici.Thanks`) now reads as a domain and is not detected, a known false negative the tests pin, because it has the shape of `jane@hdfcbank.com`. The Community build detects by pattern alone, with no context analysis, so an `@` inside a secret and a `user@host` token still read as UPI ids there; `upi_detector_4225_community_test.go` pins both on the payloads #4225 measured. The verdict consequence therefore stays on Community: a pattern-only UPI hit is critical, so under a recorded `pii=redact` the `@` secret still attaches a mandatory `field_redact`, and a caller that has not declared `field_redact@1` is still denied. That is routed to #4122, the validators' own lane.

- **An MCP connector route's refusal says it blocked** *(Community)* (#3564). `resources/query` and `tools/execute` answer every refusal with `blocked: true` beside the 403: the request pass's, the response pass's, the read-only posture's and the exfiltration limit's. Every one carried `blocked: false`, so a client reading `blocked` took a refusal for an allow. A request nothing decided still carries `blocked: false`: a malformed one (400), and one the engine could not decide (503). `check-input` and `check-output` say a refusal with `allowed: false` and are unchanged.

- **Breaking: the MCP dynamic-policy plane is retired, and its variables refuse boot** *(Community)* (PRD v11 §1.2, §1.7). The agent no longer asks the orchestrator to evaluate an organization's tenant dynamic policies for an MCP request; the anchored engine decides that pass.
  - **Migration:** remove `MCP_DYNAMIC_POLICIES_ENABLED`, `MCP_DYNAMIC_POLICIES_CONNECTORS`, `MCP_DYNAMIC_POLICIES_TIMEOUT` and `MCP_DYNAMIC_POLICIES_GRACEFUL` from every environment. Any non-empty value refuses boot, `false` included, naming the variable and the retirement (`platform/shared/retiredenv`). The shipped `docker-compose.yml` and the Community SaaS template no longer set them, and a guard fails any compose file or CloudFormation template that names a retired variable. The upgrade preflight (`scripts/deployment/v9_self_hosted_preflight.sh`) fails a deployment whose agent or orchestrator still sets one of them or a retired decision-mode variable (check 25), and its check 20 now reports segment-scoped legacy rows as deciding nothing on the enforcing planes, with no MCP per-user-token consequence.
  - **The custom-policy connector ceiling is gone.** No edition caps the connectors a policy applies to (it was 2, 5 and unlimited), and nothing returns `CONNECTOR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. The licence's `custom_policy_connectors` limit is deprecated and enforced nowhere; licence validation responses still carry it.
  - **`policy_info.dynamic_policy_info` is removed** from MCP responses.
  - **`axonflow_create_tenant_policy` reports `enforced: false`**, with an `enforcement_blocked_reason` naming PRD v11 §1.2, instead of promising the stored policy applies to MCP calls. Tenant dynamic policies no longer decide on the LLM, MAP and WCP planes: the workflow step gate, the multi-agent plane, `/api/v1/process` and plan execute are decided by the anchored engine, and a v10-authored dynamic row stops deciding there until it is imported into the typed document. Dynamic route policies still steer provider selection on `/api/v1/process`.
  - The orchestrator's `POST /api/v1/mcp/evaluate-policies` is removed too (see the entry below).
  - Removed at base `e18bc311f`: `platform/shared/policy/dynamic_evaluator.go` (the evaluator; `InitGlobalDynamicPolicyEvaluator` at `:522`), `platform/shared/policy/license_tier_source.go` and `platform/agent/license_tier_source.go` (the ceiling's licence-tier source), `platform/shared/policy/types.go:984` (`DynamicPolicyConfig`, through `CustomPolicyConnectorLimitForTier` at `:1137`), `:774` and `:1223` (`DynamicPolicyInfo`), `platform/agent/run.go:1462` (the evaluator's start), `platform/agent/mcp_v1_pro_tools.go:792` (`tenantPolicyEnforcementStatus`), and `platform/orchestrator/policy_tier_support.go:35`, `:132`, `:264` and `:458` (`CustomPolicyConnectorLimit` and `ErrCodeConnectorLimitExceeded`).

- **Breaking: the orchestrator's MCP dynamic-policy endpoint is removed** *(Community)* (#3564, PRD v11 §1.2, §1.7). `POST /api/v1/mcp/evaluate-policies` evaluated an organization's tenant dynamic policies for an MCP request. Once the agent stopped calling it, it answered only callers that reached it through the agent's proxy, with fail-open arms of its own: a missing engine answered allowed, an unknown policy type was skipped, and a rate-limit or budget policy with no limit read as allowed. The agent no longer proxies the path and the orchestrator no longer registers it.
  - **Migration:** there is no replacement route; the anchored engine decides MCP requests on the agent (`check-input`, `check_policy`, and `query`/`execute` before the tool runs). Rows of the `rate-limit`, `budget`, `time-access` and `role-access` types lose the semantics only this endpoint gave them (windowed counting, budgets, time windows, role checks). The orchestrator's database engine still loads such rows and evaluates their conditions like any other row's, and the six MCP-specific types stay valid, so such rows still read and list. The Layer-4 `anomaly` rules go with the endpoint; #4137 tracks a typed replacement.
  - **The orchestrator no longer reads `REDIS_URL`.** It configured only this endpoint's rate-limit and budget counters. The shipped `docker-compose.yml` no longer sets it on the orchestrator (the agent still uses Redis), and the orchestrator's development compose drops the Redis service that existed for it.
  - Removed: `platform/orchestrator/mcp_dynamic_policy_handler.go`, `mcp_anomaly_policy.go` and `redis_policy_store.go` with their tests, the OpenAPI path with its three schemas, the tier-gate row and the capability registry's route. `carriesStampedTenancy` moves beside `resolveGovernedScope`, its other caller.


- **Community SaaS blocks SQL injection for every organization it registers, by a recorded and audited override** (#4017). Since v11 no environment variable sets a detection action (#3961), and the Community SaaS stack runs no customer portal, so an organization registered there kept the shipped SQL-injection actions, which warn. `POST /api/v1/register` now records `sqli=block` for the organization it creates through `platform/shared/detectionposture`, the function the customer portal's detection-posture API writes through: `updated_by` is `system:community-saas-registration`, and a `DETECTION_POSTURE_SET` row goes to `admin_audit_log`, in one transaction scoped to that organization, before the credentials are returned. When the write fails the registration answers 500 and discloses no secret; the registration row it leaves cannot authenticate and is terminated by the 1-year hard-cap sweep. The endpoint mounts only under `DEPLOYMENT_MODE=community-saas`: `migrations/community-saas/088` gives that schema `admin_audit_log`, with the DDL of `migrations/enterprise/113`, and a Community deployment has no such table. `admin_audit_log` now has one writer, `platform/shared/adminaudit`.
- **A policy pack compiles to one typed organization-root document through the corpus's own action mapping** *(Community)* (#4126, PRD v11 §1.9). `platform/decision/policypack` validates a pack source (its pattern detectors and the approver pool its step-ups name), compiles each detector into one control that reads only that detector's verdict (`signal.detector.<id>`), and refuses a committed document that is not what its source compiles to. `block` compiles through `legacycompile.ActionPolicy`; `require_approval` through the new `legacycompile.ApprovalPolicy`, which the static and dynamic compilers' approval arms now call, compiling exactly what they compiled before. The committed form names the approver group without a realm, and `Instantiate` qualifies it with a deployment's realms. **Installing:** `AXONFLOW_POLICY_PACKS` names the packs a deployment installs. The agent loads each from its image at boot and refuses to start on a name the image does not carry, on a pack whose committed document is not what its source compiles to, and on any value on a Community build, which carries no pack. Activation composes each installed pack on every organization root beside the baseline permission pack, restricted to the scopes whose call sites run its detectors, and the shared engine loads the pack's detectors on every evaluation in place of any `static_policies` row under one of their ids, so a leftover row cannot report for a pack control. `/api/v1/decide` names each pack that bound as `<id>@<digest>` in `policy_packs`, on the wire and on the audit row, and the bundle digest covers it. The PEP client's `pep.DecideResponse` carries the same field. Nothing is written to `static_policies`.
- **A refusal at the organization-root policy ceiling no longer reads like the outage refusal** (#4160). A ceiling refusal and an outage refusal on this dimension (the admission ledger cannot be reached) carry the same status and the same code, so the message is what tells a caller whether to wait or to change the request, and only the outage refusal says to retry, with its `Retry-After`. The ceiling message added in #4009 ended "removing policies and retrying costs nothing"; it now says the refusal spent none of the organization's capacity and that a request with fewer policies can still be admitted. Both the typed-authoring publish and the legacy policy routes render it (`platform/orchestrator/admission_wiring.go`).
- **The portal names each action a policy governs for the operator, not by its identifier** (#3789). A registry action record now carries a required display name and an optional description, and a record without a name is refused with `DISPLAY_NAME_NOT_DECLARED`. The authoring catalog carries them as `action_labels`, outside the catalog's content digest, so neither `CatalogDigest` nor `DeploymentCatalogVersion` moves. The deployment's three actions are named Model completion, Tool call and Agent invocation, and the grant and ceiling editors (`ee/platform/customer-portal-ui/components/policies/GrantEditor.tsx` and `CeilingEditor.tsx`) show the name first, with the identifier the document carries beside it and the description on hover; a catalog without labels still shows the identifier's local part.
- **Every shipped policy carries the name of the legacy row it was compiled from, and the platform-controls panel shows it** (#4127). `pdp.Policy` gains an optional `name` (the authoring schema admits it; the decision reason text still comes from `description`). The legacy compiler records each row's name on its source reference, and the shipped corpus carries it on every system and organization-template policy, every split and `#n` variant of one row sharing the row's one name. The corpus was regenerated from a real legacy capture: 140 names added and nothing else changed, so the system corpus digest, and with it the implicit bundle digest reported on the wire, moves; the shipped-posture table records the new corpus digest. The platform-controls view and panel (`ee/platform/customer-portal-ui/components/policies/SystemControlsPanel.tsx`) show each control's name first, with its identifier beside it.
- **Every typed-policy publish, promote and rollback now writes an audit row, in the same transaction as the write itself** (PRD v11 §1.12, #4023). Before this, neither transport recorded one: the portal logged a line and the orchestrator wrote only the activation ledger. Migration `core/181` adds `typed_policy_audit` (FORCE row-level security, append-only, organization root only), and `platform/policy/authoringstore` writes its row inside the same transaction as `PutArtifact`'s artifact insert and `AppendActivation`'s append, so the portal and the orchestrator both audit by construction and a write whose row cannot be recorded does not happen. A publish row records the author, the approvers and `self_approved`, which is true wherever every approver is the author, compared by identity; an activation row records the activator, the reason and the digest it replaced. The in-process store records the same entries. Roll the binaries back before applying `181_typed_policy_audit_down.sql`: a binary that writes the table fails every publish and activation once the table is gone. The runtime legs stay in this repository: `runtime-e2e/1431_policy_path_alias/test.sh` pins the gateway's route and `runtime-e2e/3364_portal_parity/test.sh` the portal's.
- **The shipped-posture table is derived from the corpus by a test** (#4112, PRD §1.4 and acceptance §5 item 4). `platform/decision/pdp/shipped_posture.json` lists every shipped policy with its category, the scopes it runs on and its action there, the corpus's divergence facts and a reason generated from them, and the 9 shipped rows no policy is compiled from. `TestTheShippedPostureArtifactIsDerivedFromTheCorpus` (`platform/decision/activation`) computes it through the real `activation.RestrictToScope` for every declared scope and fails when the checked-in file differs, naming the input that moved: it records the sha256 of every input it reads, plus the system corpus digest.
  - **The scopes are the ones the engine restricts to, not the corpus's scope bindings.** Eight split policies of the system corpus run on fewer scopes than their bindings name, and the table lists where they run: the four `sys_admin_*` `log` variants run on no scope (dormant, revisit #3323; until #4253 they ran only on `policy_test`, the one scope whose call sites admitted `security-admin`), while their `block` variants run on `proxy_request`, which admits the category since #4253; and the four `sys_dangerous_injection_*` `redact` variants run only on `mcp:response`.
  - Each organization-template policy is listed on the scopes where the implicit bundle binds it (#4131 corrected this line, which said all 22 were listed on every scope). Each scope is tagged enforcement, operator-tool or gated (by edition or configuration), and the section for installed policy packs is empty until packs exist.
- **A Community organization can publish and activate the draft it is seeded with: policies carried from the organization template pass the authoring floors** *(Community)* (#3746, PRD §1.4, W3-K K12). All 22 organization-template policies read `signal.*`, which is Evaluation-and-up, so publication and activation refused a Community document carrying them with `ATTRIBUTE_NAMESPACE_NOT_IN_EDITION`, and a Community organization could not publish its seeded draft without dropping the destructive-command blocks. A policy carried from the template is deployment-authored and is now exempt, at publication and at activation, which share one check.
  - **The exemption is per construct, and bounded by what the template itself spends.** A policy whose id names a shipped template policy is exempt for exactly the attribute paths, obligation families and group scope that template policy spends. Tuning it over the same paths (its effect, its actions, its condition, the per-policy re-action §1.5 needs) keeps the exemption. An edit that reads another path, attaches another obligation family or scopes to a group is refused for that construct below its floor. A template policy copied under a new id is the organization's own, and an organization's own new `signal.*` constraint keeps the Evaluation floor.
  - **Only organization-root documents carry it**, because the template seeds organization documents only.
  - **Whether the template's rows decide on a given plane today is a separate question** (#4131).
- **The legacy policy routes carry a deprecation signal naming the typed route and v11.1, on every spelling** *(Community)* (#3746, PRD §1.11). v11 keeps the legacy policy READ routes as a read-only export surface (writes answer `409 LEGACY_POLICY_WRITE_FROZEN`, #4113), because four SDKs still call them and an organization must be able to export its legacy rows after upgrading. Every response from `/api/v1/static-policies`, `/api/v1/system-policies`, `/api/v1/dynamic-policies`, `/api/v1/tenant-policies`, `/api/v1/policies*`, `/api/v1/templates*` and `/api/v1/policy-overrides` now carries `Link: </api/v1/typed-policies>; rel="successor-version"` and `X-AxonFlow-Removed-In: v11.1`. From the v11.0.0 tag it also carries RFC 9745 `Deprecation: @<epoch of the tag date>`, dated by release prep through `policypath.DeprecatedSince`; a test reds once `VERSION` reaches 11.0.0 with it unset, so no guessed date ships. There is no `Sunset` until v11.1 has a date, and `/api/v1/overrides` (ADR-044) stays outside the surface until its successor, the per-policy lever, exists.
  - **Changed for header consumers:** the #1431 signal (`Deprecation: true` plus a `Link` to the renamed path) is retired. The #1431 successors are deprecated too, every family names `/api/v1/typed-policies`, and `Deprecation` is absent until the v11.0.0 date is set.
  - **One stamped registrar per binary:** the orchestrator's 19 `/policies*` and `/templates*` method-and-path pairs, the tenant family and simulation register through `registerLegacyPolicyRoutes` on one stamped subrouter, and the tenant and simulation registrars take a `legacyRouter` so they cannot be handed a router that does not stamp. The agent stamps both system-policy prefixes and the `/policy-overrides` alias ahead of authentication. A router walk in each binary drives every registered route, and a source census over `platform/` and `ee/` reds on any legacy-family registration outside a stamped registrar; the portal's own copies are declared pending removal with the legacy policy page.
  - **The API specs mark the 55 legacy operations not yet flagged `deprecated: true`**, and all three planes expose the new header to browsers.
- **Typed policy authoring is on by default: `AXONFLOW_TYPED_AUTHORING_CATALOG` unset or empty means `deployment`** *(Community)* (#4133, PRD §1.5). The variable was "deliberately not defaulted", and the shipped compose files passed it through empty, so on a stock stack every typed-authoring publish and activation answered `503 catalog_not_configured`. That failed runtime suites 3347, 3363, 3424 and 3426 on W3-G's D2 dispatches, and it made the path PRD §1.5 names as how every organization configures policy unusable out of the box.
  - **One resolver.** `authoringcatalog.Value` maps unset and empty to `deployment` in every process that reads the variable: the orchestrator route, the portal and the importer. `conformance` stays the fixture vocabulary that activation refuses by name.
  - **A value nobody recognises is still refused.** The portal (`ee/platform/customer-portal/main.go`) refuses to start, naming the variable and §1.5, rather than serving without its policy authoring routes. The orchestrator keeps its other routes and answers 503 naming the variable.
  - **The shipped files name `deployment`:** both root compose files default to it, the community-SaaS compose file and its CloudFormation orchestrator task set it, and the marketplace template's parameter already defaulted to it.

- **A block no longer stops the request pass's detectors** *(Community)*. The shared engine's request pass stopped at its first `block`, leaving every later detector unrun, and the anchored engine reads an unrun detector as unknown: a legacy `block` row it does not carry turned every request that row matched into an `unknown_constraint` refusal. Every detector now runs past a block, in the query string and in every parameter, which are walked in sorted order. The verdict, its blocking policy and reason, and the violation it records are still the first block's. The only difference a legacy reader sees: MCP `check-input`'s matched policies now also list the matches after the first block, with the verdict unchanged.

- **There is no decision mode: the ADR-065 decision plane authors every verdict on the nine scopes it enforces** *(Community)* (#3564, #4092, #3746, #3566). `/api/v1/decide`, the gateway pre-check, `/api/request`'s Phase 1, the OpenAI-compatible route, the MCP request pass (`check-input`, the MCP server's `check_policy`, and `query`/`execute` before the tool runs) the MCP response pass (`check-output`, and the response pass of MCP `query`/`execute`), the workflow step gate, the multi-agent plane and the orchestrator's response plane on `POST /api/v1/process` and plan execute are decided by the anchored engine on every deployment and edition, with no `off`, `shadow` or `enforce`, no per-organization opt-in or opt-out and no process flag (PRD v11 §1.1). `/health`'s `decision` member is `{"enforcing_planes": [...]}` and carries no mode. Every response on those scopes carries `engine` (`anchored`; until #4253, `legacy` on `/api/request` when its tier engine decided after Phase 1 approved), `subject_type` (`User`, `Client` or `Service`) and `policy_bundle` (the digest of the bundle that decided); the OpenAI-compatible route carries them as `X-AxonFlow-Engine`, `X-AxonFlow-Subject-Type` and `X-AxonFlow-Policy-Bundle`. The decision's audit row carries the same three. **`mode` is gone from the wire and from the audit row**, and nothing replaces it. Still decided by the legacy engines until W3-H cuts them over: `cowork_ingest`, `policy_test` and the orchestrator's planes; `/api/request`'s Phase 2 tier engine (`proxy_tier`) was removed by #4253.

- **Breaking: `evaluated_policies` on `/api/v1/decide` names corpus control ids** *(Community)* (PRD v11 §1.2). A shipped control is named `corpus:static_policies:<policy id>`, with the id encoded the way the decision plane encodes every identifier segment (`sys_pii_credit_card` reads `sys__pii__credit__card`), and a control the corpus splits by scope names its variant by appending the action (`corpus:static_policies:sys__pii__credit__card:warn`). The legacy row ids no longer appear there. MCP check-output's `policy_info.matched_policies` is the detector layer's and still names the row. #4127 carries the display name and version that ride beside the id.

- **Breaking: on `/api/v1/decide` an organization's redact override refuses a caller that does not declare redaction** *(Community)* (ADR-065 invariant 8; PRD v11 §1.2). Where v10 allowed the request and attached `redact_pii`, v11 refuses it as `unsupported_obligation` and names the organization's override among `evaluated_policies`: a caller that cannot discharge a mandatory redaction must not receive the content. A PEP declares what it can discharge in the capability handshake, the `X-Axonflow-PEP-Handshake` header (for redaction, the `field_redact` capability at version 1), and a declaring caller is allowed with the obligation attached. SDK releases 9.4.0 (Go, Python, TypeScript and Java) and 0.11.0 (Rust) declare it; older SDKs are refused on a redact override. Whether the same refusal applies to the shipped redact defaults on the response scopes, and not only to an organization's override, is not measured here. On Enterprise, where the circuit breaker records policy violations, a capability refusal does not feed it: an `unsupported_obligation` deny records no violation against the client on `/api/v1/decide`, the gateway pre-check, the OpenAI-compatible route or `/api/request`, as #2958 already held for its fallback gate. An enforcement point that presented an admitted handshake and is refused this way is told its capability gap again, as #3704's refusal told it: on `/api/v1/decide`, the gateway pre-check and the MCP response pass the refusal's own reason is followed by the `pep_capability_unsupported` detail and counted in `axonflow_pep_capability_refusals_total{status, type, plane}`, as on the MCP request pass; a caller that presented no handshake is unchanged.

- **A checksum validator's redaction is carried onto the verdict on `/api/v1/decide`, the AuthZEN surface and the gateway pre-check** *(Community)* (ADR-065 invariant 8; replaced by #4122). Under an organization's recorded `pii=redact` override, the Indonesian and Indian checksum validators find critical identifiers no shipped control detects (a NIK, an Aadhaar, a PAN), and with the anchored engine the only author that requirement was detected, recorded and then dropped: an allow with no obligation, the identifier forwarded unredacted. It is now a mandatory `redact_pii` obligation sourced to the validator (`indonesia_pii_protection`, `rbi_pii_protection`), judged by the same discharge rule as the engine's own: a caller that cannot discharge it is refused `unsupported_obligation`, one that can is handed it, and `legacy_validators` records `{validator, action: redaction_required}` on the response and the audit row. On the gateway pre-check the same hole already existed for organizations that had opted into the decision mode's `enforce`; it is closed here. This is a stopgap: #4122 makes the validators detector facts the engine decides from. `/api/request`, the MCP passes and the OpenAI-compatible route have no validator redaction path, before or after.

- **A caller with only a client credential is decided for that credential** *(Community)* (#4092, ADR-065 invariant 2 as amended 2026-09-11 (third), PRD v11 §1.6). On Community and Community-SaaS, and on the OpenAI-compatible route, the authenticated client credential is the principal the decision is evaluated for, recorded as `subject_type=Client`. On Community and Community-SaaS a user token is not an identity and is ignored. The OpenAI-compatible route does not honour OpenAI's `user` member as an identity. **A user token that fails verification is still refused** (401 at authentication), and the decision plane's user door refuses it too: admission is for the absence of a user identity, never for a bad one. A user token must name its issuer and its subject: one whose issuer is undeclared, or that carries no `sub`, is refused by the identity plane on every enforcing scope, where the retired mode `off` let it reach the legacy engine.

- **An organization that has published nothing is decided by its implicit bundle, and a published document keeps the baseline permission pack beside it** *(Community)* (PRD v11 §1.4). With no active typed document, an organization's requests are decided by the shipped corpus restricted to the scope, the deployment's baseline permission pack, and the organization policy template restricted to the scope, composed and signed per process and never persisted.
